limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 45,270 and 1,078,800: 88% of the 2401 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1952 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,906 against 37,650; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.
Candidates ['education'] passed the joint-test rule, but the R-learner smooth on them does not beat a constant effect by more than one SE (gain 109,035, SE 125,674); none is claimed.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: education p=0.0126 (+1613, +827, +1378, +1462 dollars per SD); parttime p=0.0656 (-4469, +1869, -1243, -3082 dollars per SD); prior_earnings p=0.164 (-2540, +6218, +1970, -634 dollars per SD); region p=0.356 (+2196, +1082, +1987, +2040 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
20.0% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 4,128 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 3,266 dollars with 90% interval [-3,054, 9,586], against the ATE 6,434. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,649.8 (train) against 25,750.0 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 5.6%. 224 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 7,879 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 4.3%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['education', 'parttime', 'prior_earnings'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
